newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Britain's ICI sees big growth in Asia.
newsitem.headline: Britain's ICI sees big growth in Asia.

text.p: Imperial Chemicals Industries Plc (ICI) said on Wednesday it aimed to boost Asia's contribution to the group's turnover to 25 percent by 2005 from 17 percent now.
"It is our intention that by year 2005, we will grow the Asian market to 25 percent on its own," Wong Hong Sze, managing director of ICI (Singapore) Pte Ltd told a news conference.
Wong said the contribution from Asia excluding Australia to the group's turnover of Singapore $22 billion (US$15.7 billion) in 1995 stood at 17 percent.
Chew Gaik Hean, chief executive of ICI Paints (Asia Pacific), said the British chemical giant planned that paint sales revenue in Asia would hit S$1 billion by year 2000.

"Sales in paints will reach S$1 billion by 2000. This represents a double digit growth for the last three-four years and we expect a continuous growth at that dimension," Chew said. He declined to give the region's current contribution.
ICI Paints produces more than one billion litres of paint a year.
Wong said the company intended to reach the S$1 billion sales target by expanding regionally in "a two-pronged approach of organic growth and acquisitions".
New plants have been built in Malaysia, Thailand and Guangzhou in China with additional ones scheduled to be opened in Bombay, Jakarta and Shanghai in 1997.
Wong said ICI Paints had also acquired operations in the Philippines and Vietnam and "will increasingly do so in other countries".
Officials said ICI has also obtained board approval to build a third plant at Chandigarh in north India.

Chew said ICI's capital investments in Asian projects in the last three to four years were estimated at around S$100 million. On its polyurethane business, the group is planning its next major expansion in Shanghai.

"Polyurethanes business is in the late process of getting the State Planning Council's permission to build the first worldscale plant in Shanghai. This will take our investments in the next five years to about S$0.6-0.7 million," said Chew Eng Soo, business director of ICI Polyurethanes (Asia Pacific).
Polyurethane products are used in the manufacture of appliances, automotive components, construction materials, furniture, footwear and a range of adhesives and encapsulants.
On Wednesday, ICI announced that ICI Paints Asia Pacific and ICI Polyurethanes Asia Pacific had been given Operational Headquarters status by Singapore's Economic Development Board.
The status gives the two companies concessionary corporate tax rates of 10 percent for an initial period of five years. The normal corporate tax is 26 percent.
